text: AWS's core model is pay-as-you-go — no upfront purchase, no fixed seat count. You're billed on compute, storage, and mostly outbound data transfer, based on actual usage.

An idle EC2 instance still costs money because it's still running, but an empty S3 bucket costs essentially nothing. The Free Tier gives bounded no-cost allowances, but exceed them and normal billing applies immediately.

Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and Spot don't change what you're running, they change how much you pay by trading flexibility for discount — up to a one-to-three-year commitment, or accepting interruption for Spot's steepest discount.
Cost Explorer shows where the money's going, and Budgets alerts you before a forgotten resource becomes a surprise bill. Next up: Chapter 3 — Users, Groups & Roles, IAM in real depth.
